question: What fish-collection context does Lam and Sia Su (2009) document for Marikina River, and can its genus-level taxon, reported coordinates, and NAST abstract be promoted to species-level occurrence or current safety information?

source.title: Total Arsenic and Total Mercury Concentrations of the Waters and Janitor Fishes (Pterygoplichthys spp.) in the Marikina River, Philippines
source.citation: Lam, J. C., & Sia Su, G. L. (2009). Total Arsenic and Total Mercury Concentrations of the Waters and Janitor Fishes (Pterygoplichthys spp.) in the Marikina River, Philippines. Journal of Applied Sciences in Environmental Sanitation, 4(1), 37-42, January-April 2009.
source.accessMethod: Reviewed the full-text mirror's title, abstract, methods, upstream/downstream localities and coordinate statements, and the relevant results/discussion for provenance and summary consistency. Separately reviewed the official NAST-hosted Transactions abstract BS-16. The article mirror identifies the Journal of Applied Sciences in Environmental Sanitation and publisher, but no publisher-hosted copy was independently verified. No article PDF, map, table, or raw measurement file was retained.
source.copyrightAndReuse: The accessible full-text mirror states that the article is open access under Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Unported (CC BY 3.0). This statement was not independently verified against a publisher-hosted copy. The NAST volume states © 2009 National Academy of Science and Technology Philippines; no item-specific open reuse license was identified for its abstract. Only concise attributed citation and methods facts are summarized; no article text, map, table, abstract, or measurement dataset is redistributed.

studyDesign.studyPurpose: Cross-sectional study of total arsenic and total mercury in river water and source-labeled janitor fish from upstream and downstream sampling areas.

sampling.fishSampleCount: Not stated in the reviewed full text.
sampling.stationAllocation: The article summarizes comparisons by upstream area (n=3) and downstream area (n=2); these table n values are not fish counts. It does not provide fish counts or taxon-by-community results for the five named communities.

coordinateAndLocalityLimits.interpretation: The article gives one coordinate pair for each broad upstream/downstream sampling area and names three upstream and two downstream communities. It does not crosswalk either pair to a particular community, trawl event, fish lot, or individual. Preserve the source strings only as research provenance; do not convert them into species-occurrence points or assume they locate every named sample.
coordinateAndLocalityLimits.vouchers: No specimen catalogue numbers, vouchers, sequence accessions, or individual sample identifiers were found in the reviewed text. This is not evidence that records do not exist elsewhere.

studyDesign.samplingLimit: The article describes a single historical sampling month and a pollutant-focused cross-sectional study, not a standardized fish-community inventory, abundance survey, or current-presence assessment.

nastAbstract.abstractTitle: Arsenic and Mercury Concentrations of the Waters and Janitor Fishes (Pterygoplichthys spp.) in the Marikina River, Philippines
nastAbstract.relationship: The official NAST Transactions abstract shares the two named authors, Marikina River, Pterygoplichthys spp. label, upstream/downstream design and June 2008 collection month with the journal article. Treat it as the likely conference summary of the same research project, not an independent survey. The conference abstract has a spelling variant for Lam's first name in its contents listing, while the abstract body and article use Jacquiline.
nastAbstract.summaryDiscrepancy: The NAST abstract matches the rounded concentration summaries printed in the journal article abstract, but the journal article results section reports different values. Preserve this within-publication abstract/results discrepancy; do not treat the NAST abstract as independent measurements or use any of the historical values as a current condition or safety threshold.
nastAbstract.meetingDateCaveat: The NAST volume is for the 31st Annual Scientific Meeting held 8-9 July 2009; this is a presentation date, not the reported June 2008 field date.
nastAbstract.decision: Link the abstract as a related publication record; count one likely field-study lineage and retain the reported-summary discrepancy.

relatedMarikinaStudies.relationship: The 2010 tissue-metal study reports 68 Pterygoplichthys spp. from four Marikina River stations, but no verified field date. Its relationship or sample overlap with the June 2008 Lam and Sia Su survey cannot be resolved from the reviewed sources.
The 2011 COI study documents unresolved P. pardalis/P. disjunctivus identity boundaries in a separate reported sample series. No specimen crosswalk links that series to the 2008 pollution study.

The 2016 life-history paper reports a July 2010-June 2011 Marikina host-fish sample under the name P. disjunctivus; this different reported period does not establish individual linkage to the 2008 sample.

reuseAndSafety.licenseDecision: The article mirror states CC BY 3.0, but original publisher access and license notice were not independently verified. The official NAST abstract has no identified item-specific open license. Do not redistribute source text, article figures, tables, or measurement values.
reuseAndSafety.safetyDecision: The source concerns historical June 2008 sampling and reports its own interpretation under cited 1990 criteria. It is not a current water-quality result, fish-consumption advisory, health-risk assessment, or fishing/legal guidance for Bangwit. Do not publish a safety badge or infer that the river or fish are safe or unsafe today.

evidenceDecision.decision: Retain as historical research-only evidence of genus-labeled Pterygoplichthys spp. collected by trawl net in June 2008 in a Marikina River upstream/downstream study covering five named communities. The article provides no fish sample count, taxon-by-community allocation, or specimen crosswalk; its area-level coordinate strings are not individual capture points. Do not add a species assertion, occurrence row, coordinate, geometry, image, current safety claim, or public app projection.

nonClaims: Pterygoplichthys spp. is a genus-level label and does not establish P. pardalis, P. disjunctivus, or a particular hybrid or species identity.
The article does not report fish sample counts, fish-by-community counts, voucher identifiers, or exact station-to-specimen mapping.
The two reported upstream/downstream coordinate pairs are not community-specific capture locations and do not support occurrence points for any species.
The NAST abstract is not an independent survey confirmation; its rounded summary matches the journal abstract, while the journal results section reports different values.
The historical pollution study does not establish current fish presence, abundance, fish-consumption safety, water safety, catchability, fishing access, or legal harvest.
nextActions: Keep the journal article and NAST abstract as one likely research lineage and do not add species-level, occurrence, geometry, or safety content.
Only revise the genus-level and site-level limits if source-linked vouchers, fish sample lists, or station-specific capture records become available.
Continue NCR coverage discovery across freshwater, brackish, marine and wetland lanes; NCR, CALABARZON, and Luzon remain incomplete.
